new_interpretation: The immutable public Qwen checkpoint stores the tied embedding once and has no lm_head.weight entry, but Transformers re-ties lm_head.weight to the input embedding after loading and PyTorch state_dict exposes registered aliases. The public CPO mask builder therefore expands the mask namespace beyond the serialized checkpoint namespace.

The public trainer precomputes int64 nonzero indices for every saved mask key before iterating named_parameters, so a dead tied alias consumes mask, reference and index storage even though no trainer hook can consume that alias key.

The exact Qwen3-VL model source registers only two explicit RoPE buffers and both are persistent=False; no persistent floating buffer was found in the audited Qwen3-VL, PreTrainedModel or GradientCheckpointingLayer sources. Therefore the tied alias is the source-evident trainer-invisible floating state for this exact stack, subject to the scope limits below.

Public CPO 4B training sets freeze_vision_tower=False, freeze_llm=False and freeze_merger=False, so the tied embedding is trainable. Actual nonzero top-10 support still requires a real checkpoint diff and is not assumed.
scope_limits: No Qwen3-VL-4B model was loaded in this invocation.
No PyTorch 2.8 binary execution occurred; environment download failed because DNS/package download was unavailable.
The 10-percent dead-alias payload is conditional on the selected embedding movements being nonzero; the builder discards zero-valued top-k positions.
The Hugging Face revision is the current public immutable revision observed during this run, not proof of the exact local model revision used by the CPO authors.
No claim is made about unreleased code used for paper tables.
